saints.name: St. Vitus
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A boy martyr of the early Church, one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers invoked in sickness…
biography: According to his legend, Vitus was the young son of a pagan senator of Sicily, secretly brought to the faith by his tutor Modestus and his nurse Crescentia. Fleeing his father's anger, the three came to Lucania and there died of their tortures in the persecution of Diocletian, about the year 303, Vitus being yet a boy.

Their cult is ancient: the fifth-century Martyrology of Jerome joins their names in Sicily, and Gregory the Great speaks of a monastery of Vitus there. In 836 some of his relics were carried from Saint-Denis to the abbey of Corvey in Saxony, whence his devotion spread through Germany; in 925 King Henry I gave relics of Vitus to Wenceslaus of Bohemia, still enshrined in Prague's cathedral of St. Vitus.

Numbered among the Fourteen Holy Helpers, he is invoked against epilepsy and against the nervous disorder that bears his name: for on his feast the Germans danced before his statue, whence he became the patron of dancers, and the dancing sickness came to be called St. Vitus's Dance.
saints.knownFor: One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers; patron of dancers.
